In a very simplified explanation, wordpress is a template that gives you a fully functional website.

The benefit is that you don't have to build everything from scratch. Right out of the box:

  • Your login page is example.com/wp-admin
  • Your images and videos are stored at example.com/wp-content
  • etc etc

The drawback is... well, anyone familiar with wordpress knows where your login page is. That's not good. If enough people try to guess the password then eventually someone will get it right.

The right way to handle this is to prevent people from accessing those pages. Put up some kind of gate or protection around them.

You can see who handles this well and who does not by searching duckduckgo for something like "sites that use wordpress", and then appending "/wp-admin" or "/wp-content" to the end of the URL. But don't. For the sake of legal protection, don't do that.

In most cases, example.com/wp-content should redirect you to a "not found" page or something similar. In this case, whoever runs Shareblue.com neglected to perform a pretty basic function of their job, and as a result the site opens it's proverbial doors and says "sure, go for it, take whatever you want" .
